INTERAGENCY AUTISM COORDINATING COMMITTEE (IACC)
At-a-Glance
2021-2022 AUTISM RESEARCH PORTFOLIO ANALYSIS REPORT
The 2021-2022 IACC Autism Research Portfolio Analysis Report provides comprehensive 
information about the status of autism research funding among federal agencies and 
private research organizations in the United States. This At-a-Glance version provides a 
summary of key findings included in the report. The full report can be found here: 
https://iacc.hhs.gov/publications/portfolio-analysis/2022/ 
Who funded autism research in 2022?
33 funders 
provided funding data 
for this report.
15 federal agencies
18 private organizations
For more information about the IACC, please visit: https://iacc.hhs.gov/ 
Thank you to all funders who contributed to this report!

• U.S. autism research was funded at the highest ever level in 2022 ($456.1 million).
• Federal agencies accounted for 78.4% of total funding ($357.4 million).
• Private organizations accounted for 21.6% ($98.6 million).
• Overall funding for autism research increased by 4.4% ($19.0 million) from 2021 to 2022.
• Private investment notably increased by 36.7% ($26.5 million) from 2021 to 2022.

The Seven Question Areas of the IACC Strategic Plan
How can we improve identification of autism?
What is the biology underlying autism?
What are the genetic and environmental factors that contribute to autism and its 
co-occurring conditions?
Which interventions will improve health and well-being?
What services and supports are needed to maximize health and well-being?
How can we address the needs of people on the autism spectrum throughout the lifespan?
How do we expand and enhance research infrastructure systems to meet the needs of the 
autism community?
Examples of research topics: diagnostic and screening tools, early signs and biomarkers, improve 
access to early diagnosis, spectrum of characteristics
Examples of research topics: brain structure and function, cognitive studies, language development 
and communication, co-occurring conditions, molecular pathways, sensory and motor function
Examples of research topics: gene-environment interactions, genetic factors, environmental factors
Examples of research topics: augmentative and alternative communication (AAC), behavioral, 
educational, pharmacological/medical, dietary, occupational, and technology-based interventions
Examples of research topics: community participation, education, service delivery, practitioner 
training, safety, improve service access and outcomes
Examples of research topics: employment, housing, daily life skills, health outcomes, health care 
systems, transition to adulthood, postsecondary outcomes, aging
Examples of research topics: data tools, prevalence, research infrastructure, research workforce
Which areas of autism research were funded?
Projects were funded within all seven Question areas of the 2021-2023 IACC Strategic Plan.
Which areas of autism research experienced the greatest growth?
Biology
• The largest portion of the autism research 
portfolio, has grown by over $150 million 
since 2008, but flattened in recent years
Genetic and Environmental Factors
• Funding increased by $18.9 million from 
2021 to 2022
Interventions
• Notably high proportion (43.7%) of funds 
devoted to new projects
Services and Supports
• Funding in recent years is nearly 10 times 
the 2008 level, reaching $46.5 million in 
2021
Lifespan
• Grew from 8 projects in 2008 to 156 
projects in 2022 (> 1,000%)
